subject: Onboarding: model shortlist + context & token scoping for ClearLedger
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Tang <emily@clearledger.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: model shortlist + context & token scoping for ClearLedger

Emily — great to meet last week. I’m taking over the onboarding handoff and want to align on model choices and the token/workload sizing we need to run the pilot. Goal: give CS + infra a concise shortlist and a proposed capacity reservation so we can schedule a tech sync.

Quick asks (can reply inline):
- Primary objective: accuracy of analytics summarization vs latency sensitivity?
- Typical user request: please paste two real prompt examples (sanitized).
- Expected average and 95th percentile tokens for request+response.
- Peak concurrent requests (peak hour) and average QPS.
- Any must-have context length (e.g., 4k / 16k / 32k)?

I attached a small workbook to capture token estimates and traffic curves; please drop sample prompts in prompt_samples.txt if that’s easier.

Initial thought from our side: produce a model shortlist covering a low-latency 8k-ish variant, a quality 32k variant, and a compact quantized 8k variant for cost testing. We’ll also include recommendations for prefix caching if you have repetitive context in requests.

Proposed next step: quick 30-min sync Thurs or Fri to review the workbook and pick a pilot model.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachment: onboarding_token_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Emily Tang <emily@clearledger.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model shortlist + context & token scoping for ClearLedger

Marissa — thanks, and thanks for the workbook. Answers below and I’ve attached sanitized prompt examples.

Primary objective: high precision on accounting reconciliation summarization (accuracy > low hallucination > latency). We need human-review-grade outputs for 80% of cases.

Sample prompts (see prompt_samples.txt): two short examples — one single-turn summary (~40 tokens input) and one multi-doc merge (~800 tokens input).

Token profile (estimates):
- Average request tokens (user input): 60
- Average response tokens: 140
- Typical end-to-end per-request: ~200 tokens
- 95th percentile single request (multi-doc merges): up to 1,800 tokens

Traffic:
- Average steady-state QPS: 0.8–1.2
- Peak hour QPS: 18
- Peak concurrent requests (during a batch spike): ~40
- Monthly token estimate (current pilot scope): ~3.2M tokens/month

Context length need: for multi-doc merges we’d like 16k to start; 32k would be ideal later in production.

We attached the sample prompts and a basic traffic_curve.csv that shows the diurnal/weekly pattern.

Let us know availability for Thurs 10:30 or Fri 11:00 PT.

—Emily
Emily Tang, Head of Product
ClearLedger
emily@clearledger.com

Attachment: prompt_samples.txt (text file stub), traffic_curve.csv (CSV stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model shortlist + context & token scoping for ClearLedger

Looping in infra notes. Emily — thanks for the breakdown, that’s very helpful. A few practical notes from serving and model ops: 

1) Model shortlist (recommendation for pilot):
   - Candidate A: high-throughput 8k quantized variant (best cost baseline)
   - Candidate B: 16k non-quantized mid-tier (balance of context and accuracy)
   - Candidate C: 32k quality variant (for multi-doc merges; higher cost)

2) Runtime configuration suggestions:
   - Enable KV/prefix caching for common ledger headers — will save tokens and latency on repeated queries.
   - Suggest baseline multiplexing/batching window = 5–10ms to hit cost targets without violating latency SLOs.

3) Token/throughput sanity check: your 3.2M/month pilot looks right for average traffic; we’ll size Dedicated pilot capacity to handle 3x peak concurrency with headroom.

4) Quantization tradeoffs: we’ll run a quick eval on your prompt samples to measure quality delta (A/B with Candidate A vs B). If loss is <2% for your accuracy metric, we’ll push quantized A as default for cost savings.

Question: What’s the 95th or 99th percentile latency requirement you need for human-review workflows? That defines whether we pin on lower-latency hardware or accept batching.

I’ll prepare a short CSV with modeled token spend across the three candidates once we confirm latency SLOs.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Emily Tang <emily@clearledger.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jul 2025 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model shortlist + context & token scoping for ClearLedger

Ben — thanks. Clarifying SLA expectations:
- Our business requirement is human-review turnaround; we’d like 95th percentile end-to-end latency for single-turn requests below 700ms and 99th below 1.5s.
- For the larger multi-doc merges we can accept higher latency (95th up to 2.5s) but prefer <1s when using the 16k pipeline.

Traffic curve: attached (traffic_curve.csv) shows sustained spikes for 10–15 minutes several times per day; peak concurrency numbers stand.

We are targeting the pilot to start with the 16k mid-tier (Candidate B) and evaluate Candidate A for cost. If Candidate B meets accuracy with acceptable latencies, we’ll trial Candidate C on a smaller subset for the large merges.

Available for Fri 11:00 PT — let’s confirm calendar invite.

Thanks,
Emily

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Tang <emily@clearledger.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model shortlist + context & token scoping for ClearLedger — next steps

Emily — great, thanks for the clarity. Quick summary and action items before Friday’s sync at 11:00 PT: 

Summary decisions:
- Pilot model: Candidate B (16k non-quantized) as default for pilot.
- Cost trial: Candidate A (8k quantized) to be tested against a sample of 10k requests to measure accuracy delta.
- Large merges: Candidate C (32k) reserved for a targeted subset (10% of merges) if we see regression on 16k.
- Latency SLOs: 95th < 700ms (single-turn); multi-doc 95th target < 2.5s.

Action items:
1) Redwood: run A/B eval on prompt_samples.txt and deliver a CSV with token/spend model and expected P95 latencies for each candidate (attachment: model_shortlist_and_token_estimates.csv). Owner: Ben. ETA: EOD Thu.
2) ClearLedger: confirm sanitized sample set for the 10k request accuracy trial and grant access to the sample repo link. Owner: Emily. ETA: Thu EOD.
3) Agree cadence for monitoring: weekly token & quality report during pilot; escalation path to account exec if accuracy regresses >3%. Owner: Marissa.

I’ll drop the calendar invite for Fri 11:00 PT and attach the model_shortlist_and_token_estimates.csv once Ben uploads it to the shared drive. Looking forward to the sync.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachment: model_shortlist_and_token_estimates.csv (generated stub)
